review_method: Re-review all eight categories and nine vetoes using dated harness raw/evidence, reconcile latest/checkpoint differences, recompute cash scenarios and reverse expectations, refresh dated prices, retain unaffected judgments and document every score change. No macro-score mixing.
portfolio_context: Actual holdings, taxes and risk budget are not provided. Research completion does not authorize a purchase. Macro conditions affect pacing/risk budget, not the company-quality score.
structural_thesis: TransMedics is building an integrated organ-transplant platform around OCS warm perfusion, NOP clinical/logistics coordination and an owned/controlled aviation network. If execution succeeds, the system can expand donor-organ utilization and become embedded in transplant-center workflows; the trade-off is materially higher capital intensity than a conventional medical-device model.
current_finding: Q2 revenue grew 21% YoY to $189.9M and FY2026 guidance remains $737M-$757M, but H1 operating income fell 42% to $37.0M and H1 OCF of $41.8M did not cover $43.7M of PP&E purchases before SBC and finance-lease economics. Product gross margin remains strong while service/logistics mix grows faster and carries lower margin.
capital_and_survival: June cash was $472.7M, but capital claims include $460M principal of 2028 convertibles, bank debt, roughly $347.7M finance-lease liability, aircraft/logistics requirements and $200M-$240M of expected headquarters capex through 2030. The company states liquidity is sufficient for at least 12 months, but long-run owner-cash conversion remains the key underwriting question.

evidence: OCS/NOP combines organ preservation, clinical workflow and logistics rather than selling a stand-alone disposable device.
PAD Aviation extends the model toward a dedicated European transplant-air-logistics network, increasing the addressable workflow controlled by TransMedics.
counter_evidence: International replication is not yet economically proven and adding aviation/logistics raises fixed-cost, regulatory and execution complexity.
missing_data: Long-run transplant-volume uplift attributable specifically to NOP/European logistics versus secular transplant growth remains incomplete.

evidence: Q2 revenue rose 21% and management attributes growth primarily to higher OCS utilization in liver and heart plus logistics services.
OCS offers transplant centers the ability to preserve, assess and transport donor organs in a coordinated workflow, addressing a high-value clinical bottleneck.
counter_evidence: Public reporting does not provide center-level ROI, retention or procedure-level economics sufficient to quantify standardized customer payback.
missing_data: Center-level utilization cohorts, procedure economics and independent reimbursement/payback data.

evidence: Integration of FDA-cleared OCS technology, NOP logistics and dedicated aviation can create workflow switching costs and operational know-how that are harder to replicate than the device alone.
Product gross margin was about 77% in Q2, indicating pricing/value capture remains strong in the core product layer.
counter_evidence: The expanding service layer had roughly 35% Q2 gross margin and may dilute consolidated economics even while strengthening the network moat.
Clinical/regulatory alternatives and cold-storage or competing perfusion approaches remain credible long-run substitutes.
missing_data: Organ-specific competitive win/loss data and durable center-level retention statistics.

evidence: Revenue continues to grow above 20% and product economics are attractive.
Management is investing in OCS Kidney, Gen 3.0, clinical programs and logistics that could create additional growth vectors.
counter_evidence: H1 OCF was $41.842M versus $43.749M PP&E purchases; OCF-PPE was -$1.907M before $18.558M SBC and lease economics.
H1 operating income fell to $37.033M from $64.010M as growth investment and service mix compressed operating leverage.
missing_data: Normalized aircraft maintenance/replacement capex, lease principal, PAD economics and organ-specific contribution margins are needed for a clean incremental-ROIC estimate.

evidence: Management raised the lower end of 2026 revenue guidance in August and reiterated $737M-$757M on September 10.
Fernando Araujo, with large-scale healthcare and industrial finance experience, was appointed CFO effective September 21, potentially strengthening finance infrastructure during global scaling.
counter_evidence: The inventory-movement material weakness remained unremediated at June 30, so disclosure controls were not effective.
The owned/leased aircraft network, PAD expansion and headquarters build require disciplined capital allocation that has not yet produced demonstrated per-share owner-cash leverage.

재고 이동 내부통제의 중대한 취약점이 미시정이고 H1 OCF가 유형자산 취득에도 못 미친다. 항공·본사 투자와 전환채/리스 부담에 대한 회수 증거가 부족하다. 9/21 취임 예정 CFO의 경력과 매출 가이던스 재확인은 통제 개선이나 자본배분 성과가 아니므로 해당 항목을 6→5로 보수적으로 재평가한다. 부정회계가 확인됐다는 뜻은 아니며 회계 veto는 INVESTIGATE를 유지한다.
missing_data: Evidence that the new inventory controls have operated effectively for a sufficient period and formal remediation of the material weakness.

evidence: Cash was $472.675M at June 30 and management stated existing liquidity should fund operations, capex and debt service for at least 12 months.
The company remains GAAP profitable and raised/reiterated annual revenue guidance.
counter_evidence: Capital claims include $460M convertible principal due 2028, bank debt, about $347.7M finance-lease liability and $200M-$240M expected headquarters capex through 2030.
The aviation/logistics strategy increases fixed and replacement-capital requirements compared with an asset-light medtech model.
missing_data: Detailed multi-year aircraft replacement schedule, PAD financing terms and normalized maintenance-capital requirements.

evidence: At the preserved $85.04 reference price, Base value is about $110.47 per share, roughly 30% above the reference.
With the Base owner-margin path and capital adjustments fixed, the reverse model requires only about 7.8% annual revenue growth for years 2-10, implying year-10 revenue of roughly $1.77B.
2026-09-12 재검증: 관측가격 82.18 USD; Bear/Base/Bull 17.1790/110.4719/362.7635. 모형 가정·원자료 기준은 valuation.json에 보존.
counter_evidence: The valuation advantage exists only if owner-cash margin eventually reaches about 16%; current H1 owner-cash conversion is negative after PP&E and SBC.
Base value has substantial terminal-value dependence and is highly sensitive to margin, capital intensity and discount-rate assumptions.
missing_data: PAD contribution, mature service margins and normalized aviation capex remain insufficiently disclosed for a high-confidence intrinsic-value estimate.

evidence: Bull value is about $362.76, more than four times the reference price, if OCS/NOP becomes a broader transplant platform with operating leverage.
The mechanical Bear/Bull break-even Bull weight is below 20%, indicating attractive modeled upside asymmetry.
2026-09-12 재검증: 관측가격 82.18 USD; Bear/Base/Bull 17.1790/110.4719/362.7635. 모형 가정·원자료 기준은 valuation.json에 보존.
counter_evidence: Bear value is about $17.18, nearly 80% below the reference price; capital intensity, regulatory setbacks, control failures or slower organ adoption can produce severe permanent impairment.
missing_data: Real-world scenario probabilities are unknown and should not be inferred from the mechanical break-even calculation.

evidence: Inventory-movement controls were materially weak and disclosure controls remained ineffective at June 30, although management states the financial statements are fairly presented and new controls were implemented during Q2.
items.resolution_needed: Require sufficient operating history and testing of new controls followed by formal remediation disclosure; reopen immediately if misstatements or broader control deficiencies emerge.

evidence: The company is profitable, has $472.7M cash and says current liquidity is sufficient for at least 12 months.
items.resolution_needed: Reopen if aviation/HQ/PAD commitments exceed internally generated cash and force repeated external equity or debt funding.

evidence: No evidence in the reviewed period indicates structurally excessive shareholder dilution; the valuation uses a diluted share proxy to avoid ignoring convertibles.
items.resolution_needed: Track SBC, convertibles and any equity financing for aviation or international expansion on a per-share basis.

evidence: Growth is tied to OCS utilization and services in clinically valuable transplant workflows rather than subsidy-driven customer acquisition.
items.resolution_needed: Reopen if utilization growth requires material pricing concessions or logistics losses that do not improve with scale.

evidence: H1 OCF did not cover PP&E before SBC, while operating income fell despite 21% revenue growth; large aviation and HQ investment obscure incremental ROIC.
items.resolution_needed: Require at least two reporting periods of improving owner cash per diluted share and evidence that service/logistics investment earns acceptable returns.

evidence: OCS utilization, NOP integration and European logistics expansion currently point to widening workflow control rather than moat contraction.
items.resolution_needed: Reopen if transplant-center adoption stalls, reimbursement weakens or competitors displace OCS in major indications.

evidence: The reference price is below modeled Base and the reverse model requires only ~7.8% revenue growth for years 2-10 if mature owner-cash economics are achieved.
items.resolution_needed: Reopen if the price rises materially without corresponding improvement in owner-cash conversion or if Base margin assumptions prove unrealistic.

evidence: The company discloses dependence on a limited number of customers and the economic thesis remains concentrated in OCS/NOP adoption, particularly liver and heart workflows.
items.resolution_needed: Track customer/center concentration, organ mix and the success of heart, lung, kidney and international expansion in diversifying the revenue base.

evidence: Bear value is roughly 80% below the reference and large fixed/capital claims can impair equity value even without insolvency if growth or owner-cash margins disappoint.
items.resolution_needed: Require formal control remediation, demonstrated per-share cash conversion and continued evidence of clinical/commercial adoption before any purchase authorization.

reverse_expectations.growth_basis: Year-1 revenue anchor fixed; uniform growth years 2-10 (milestone paths retain fixed capital costs).
reverse_expectations.warning: Conditional on Base margins, capital claims and terminal assumptions; not an observable unique market forecast.

red_team.independence: Same analyst/model performed the red team; this is adversarial self-review, not an independent committee opinion.

attacks.attack: NOP is becoming an airline/logistics business with medtech branding, structurally lowering returns on capital.
attacks.response: The service layer may strengthen the moat, but current cash conversion validates the concern; no high ROIC assumption is granted until aircraft/logistics economics improve.

attacks.attack: Liver concentration is masking weak heart/lung adoption and leaves the thesis dependent on one organ category.
attacks.response: Diversification through heart/lung trials, kidney and international NOP remains a required evidence gate; fatal concentration stays INVESTIGATE.

attacks.attack: The inventory-control material weakness signals deeper finance-process problems.
attacks.response: Possible. Management has implemented controls but formal remediation is absent; management/accounting integrity remains INVESTIGATE rather than PASS.

attacks.attack: Revenue growth is low-quality because services grow faster at much lower gross margin than products.
attacks.response: Service margin is lower, but integrated logistics can increase OCS utilization and switching costs. The test is future consolidated owner cash, not service gross margin alone.

attacks.attack: The $460M convertibles plus finance leases and HQ spending create hidden leverage that the market underestimates.
attacks.response: All are treated as capital claims; the diluted share proxy avoids ignoring conversion and the analysis does not treat current cash as excess distributable capital.

attacks.attack: PAD Aviation international expansion will consume cash before generating meaningful revenue.
attacks.response: This is plausible and PAD economics are not modeled as free upside. Financial contribution remains unknown and is a monitoring item.

attacks.attack: Management is overinvesting because Q2 operating margin fell sharply while revenue rose.
attacks.response: The burden of proof is on management. The score remains only 6/10 and incremental ROIC 8/15 until operating leverage and owner cash recover.

attacks.attack: The Base valuation assumes 16% mature owner-cash margin even though current owner cash after PP&E and SBC is negative.
attacks.response: Accepted. This is the central valuation dependency and why the positive Base gap does not translate into STARTER status.

attacks.attack: Legal/regulatory or aviation-safety events could disrupt the integrated network and create nonlinear downside.
attacks.response: The model's wide Bear case and permanent-loss veto explicitly retain this tail risk; no probability precision is claimed.

attacks.attack: A new CFO shortly after unresolved controls could indicate organizational stress rather than strengthening.
attacks.response: The transition is treated neutrally-to-cautiously. It is not counted as remediation; only future tested controls and disciplined capital deployment can improve the management score.

completion_gate.scope: Research composition and audit lineage complete; unresolved facts and veto investigations are NOT marked resolved.

source_quality.primary_sources: SEC Q2 10-Q and company IR/news releases are the principal factual sources.
source_quality.secondary_sources: September 10 market price is a secondary reference only and is not exchange-audited by the harness.
source_quality.limitations: No independent transplant-center cohort economics, PAD transaction economics or fully normalized aircraft maintenance/replacement cash data were available.

falsifiers: The inventory-control material weakness remains unresolved after a reasonable remediation period or expands into broader accounting deficiencies.
OCS/NOP utilization grows but owner cash per diluted share fails to improve for multiple reporting periods.
Heart/lung/kidney/international expansion fails to diversify the economics while liver or major-center adoption weakens.
Service/logistics margin and aircraft capital needs prevent consolidated mature owner-cash margin from approaching the mid-teens assumed in Base.
increase_evidence: Formal remediation of the inventory-control material weakness with tested operating effectiveness.
At least two reporting periods of improving OCF after PP&E, SBC and recurring aircraft/lease capital requirements on a diluted per-share basis.
Evidence that PAD/European NOP and heart/lung/kidney programs broaden revenue without structurally diluting consolidated owner-cash margins.
A continued valuation discount to Base after the above evidence strengthens; price decline alone is insufficient.
sell_evidence: A material accounting/control failure, major OCS clinical/regulatory impairment or logistics safety/regulatory event that damages the platform thesis.
Persistent negative owner-cash conversion while capital commitments continue to rise.
Loss of major transplant-center adoption or reimbursement economics that undermines OCS/NOP utilization.
Valuation moves to require Bull-like execution without corresponding per-share cash evidence.
